bugs.summary: R CMD check should flag incorrect S4 metadata when a plain function overwrites a generic
bugs.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
I happened upon two packages, {raster} and {GenomicRanges}, where an S4 generic was accidentally overwritten by a plain function:

```
# in package PKG
setGeneric("foo", \(x) standardGeneric("foo"))
foo <- function(x) x
```

This creates a package whose S4 metadata is broken:

```
ns = getNamespace("PKG")

"foo" %in% getGenerics(ns)
#> [1] TRUE   (because .__T__foo:PKG exists)

isGeneric("foo", where=ns)
#> [1] FALSE  (because ns$foo is a plain closure)

getGeneric("foo", where=ns)
#> NULL

showMethods("foo", where=ns)
#> Function "foo":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>

findMethodSignatures("foo", where=ns)
# Error in methods@arguments : 
#   no applicable method for `@` applied to an object of class "list"
# In addition: Warning message:
# In findMethods(...) : non-generic function 'foo' given to findMethods()
```

There are numerous other weird behaviors we can generate cascading from here, many of which would be smoked out quickly, but others can be subtle. I think it's unlikely that an _exported_ method with this problem would survive very long, so I would guess this is mainly restricted to internal generics.

I'm not sure the best place in `R CMD check` to place such a consistency check (maybe `checking R code for possible problems`?), but it does seem like a good candidate to be flagged.

[1] https://github.com/rspatial/raster/issues/342
[2] https://github.com/Bioconductor/GenomicRanges/issues/101

comments.creator: Kurt.Hornik
